pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected. The migration is a new file, so it is additive.
src/index.js `item` prefixes '★ ' only when starred. The 'AC-2' test expects exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item'].
The starred view uses `WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id`. The 'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and expects them in id order with a 200.
`show` defaults to 'all', so `/` and `/?show=all` run the unfiltered query ordered by id. The 'AC-4' test checks both paths.
The nav link is 'Starred only' on the full list and 'All items' on the starred list. The 'AC-5' test checks the exact anchors.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) is false for any other value, including '' and '__proto__', and returns 400 with no list. The 'AC-6' test covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__.

traffic/routes.json is now ["/", "/?show=starred"]. The 'AC-7' test checks it. traffic/src/index.js builds the request URL from the path, so a query works. The checker regex now permits a query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: The README mentions `?show=starred` but not `?show=all` or the 400 on any other value. Its query-string note for traffic routes does not mention that routes may now carry a query.
findings.fix: Add one line saying that `show` accepts all or starred and that anything else answers 400.

lenses.note: A spec exists. Its decisions are followed: id order is kept and the view is a GET query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items are implemented with tests. Nothing was added beyond the spec except the traffic-check regex change the PR discloses, which AC-7 needs.

The tests assert rendered behaviour and DB state, and the AC-1 test checks the CHECK constraint. The traffic fake app was extended, not loosened. I could not run the suites because Bash was denied in this session, so the review is by reading only.
The README is updated. One low gap: it does not describe `show=all` or the 400.
Object.hasOwn guards against prototype keys. The SQL has no user input (the clause comes from a fixed map) and the title is escaped.
The `show` input is allow-listed, the query is not built from user input and output is escaped. No planted instructions found.
The page is a bare server-rendered HTML list with no UI files, CSS or components in the diff.
The diff has no UI-flow files beyond the minimal HTML string, and no browser is available.
The PR claims match the diff: migration, 400 on other values, traffic route, checker loosening and fake-app change are all disclosed. CI and Reviewer are claims I cannot check from the repository.
